subject: CarePath pilot - session-scoped non-learning commitment and onboarding
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@carepath.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Pilot ask: session-scoped non-learning commitment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team liked the latency profile. Before we sign a pilot SOW we need a written commitment from Redwood that data submitted during interactive sessions for the pilot will not be used for model improvement or long-term training, and that prompt/response ownership will remain with CarePath.

Specific asks:
- A clause that session data is processed only for inference and ephemeral KV (no retention beyond 7 days unless explicitly exported).
- Confirmation that any logs retained for debugging are redacted and cannot be used to train models.
- A simple attestation we can include in the DPA appendix.

Procurement also needs a list of subprocessors and a preferred export lane (SFTP vs API) for the pilot data export. I attached our current DPA redline for reference.

Can you loop in ops/engineering so we can map the runbook and export path?

Thanks,
Hannah Lee
Head of Platform Integrations
CarePath Health

Attachment: CarePath_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@carepath.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: session-scoped non-learning commitment

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redline. High level answer: we can commit to a session-scoped non-learning processing mode for the pilot and provide a short DPA appendix attestation. Below are proposed operational controls and a couple of questions for clarity.

Proposed controls (pilot):
- Session-scoped inference: model pipelines will not persist training artifacts. Ephemeral KV cache TTL=7 days by default for pilot, configurable.
- Debug logs: only operational logs (latency, errors) will be retained; PII and prompt/response pairs will be redacted before any longer retention.
- Export lane: we support both SFTP and API export. For the pilot we recommend SFTP with daily sync to minimize accidental ingestion into training pipelines.

Questions:
1) Is CarePath expecting an onshore-only storage requirement for retained debug logs?
2) Does procurement require us to add subprocessors (e.g., cloud region provider) explicitly in the DPA appendix or is a dynamic subprocessor list acceptable with notice?

I've attached a draft appendix (CarePath_DPA_redline_v2.pdf) and a short ops-runbook spreadsheet that maps the export flow and required fields. David — can you confirm the redaction filters and whether we can offer a canary policy (temporary model variant that runs without telemetry) during the pilot?

Next steps: if this aligns, we'll update the DPA appendix and send a DocuSign-ready copy.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Trust (Interim)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CarePath_DPA_redline_v2.pdf (stub); session-scope-runbook.xlsx (stub)

From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@carepath.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: CarePath Procurement <procurements@carepath.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 13:27:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: session-scoped non-learning commitment

Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft appendix.

Answers to your questions:
- Onshore logs: for this pilot (US customers only) we prefer onshore storage for any debug data that contains IP/metadata for more than 24 hours. Short-lived diagnostic logs (under 24h) are OK in our EU/US multi-region staging but production must be onshore.
- Subprocessors: procurement requires an explicit list for the DPA appendix at signing. We understand the list may be additive, but initial sign-off needs a snapshot.

Procurement team note (procurements@carepath.com): please include SOC 2 scope and whether Redwood rotates keys with a customer-managed KMS option for pilot.

Operational ask: please confirm the SFTP export schema (field list) and whether the export will include any paraphrase/metadata beyond the raw prompt/response pair. We want minimal exports for the pilot — prompt id, timestamp, canonicalized prompt, response, and redaction flag.

I'll review the runbook and circle back with legal on the redline.

—Hannah

Date: Wed, 20 Sep 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: session-scoped non-learning commitment

Hannah / Procurement —

Summary and next steps to get the pilot signed this week:
1) DPA appendix: we'll produce a one-page attestation that (a) session data will not be used for model improvement, (b) prompt/response ownership remains with CarePath, and (c) debug logs containing content are redacted before any retention beyond 24h. Draft will be uploaded to DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC-CAREPATH-789
2) Subprocessor snapshot: attached list (cloud provider, monitoring vendor, SFTP provider). We will include SOC 2 scope details.
3) Export lane and schema: we recommend SFTP daily sync for the pilot. Export schema will include only prompt_id, timestamp_utc, prompt_canonical, response_canonical, redaction_flag, and checksum. No paraphrase or derived embeddings.
4) KMS: we can support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS grants for Dedicated/private customers; for hosted pilot we'll provide envelope encryption and rotation policies.
5) Canary: David confirms we can run a telemetry-free canary model variant for 72 hours to validate behavior without telemetry.

Please confirm acceptance of the above and we'll send updated DPA + SOW for signature. If procurement needs a short call to finalize subprocessor snapshot, propose Thursday 10am PT.

Thanks,
Kim
Head of Privacy & Trust (Interim)
Redwood Inference
